title: Salvation and Grace - Episode 3: Buried guilt, rising grace

parts.style: warm, gentle late-night welcome, a soft smile in the voice, speaking slowly
parts.text: Welcome back to Salvation and Grace. <chuckle> I'm Sarah Mitchell. <short pause> This is our third evening together... <short pause> and tonight's story begins with a king who kept a secret.
It's a story about guilt that stays buried for years... <short pause> and grace that rises higher.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: You know what it feels like to carry something hidden. <short pause> A word you said that hurt someone. <short pause> A choice you made that you can't undo. <short pause> A season of your life you'd rather no one knew about. <short pause> You've moved on, but it's still there, beneath the surface.
King David knew that feeling. <short pause> He had sinned, and for a long time he kept silent about it. <short pause> He describes what that silence cost him.
When I kept silence, my bones waxed old through my roaring all the day long. For day and night thy hand was heavy upon me: my moisture is turned into the drought of summer. <long pause>
David's body felt the weight of what he wouldn't name. <short pause> His bones wasted. <short pause> His moisture dried up. <short pause> Day and night, God's hand was heavy on him.

Guilt doesn't stay quiet just because we are. <short pause> It finds other ways to speak. <short pause> It speaks in weariness that sleep doesn't fix. <short pause> In a tightness in your chest when you remember. <short pause> In the distance you feel from God.
But then David did something. <short pause> He stopped hiding.
I acknowledged my sin unto thee, and mine iniquity have I not hid. I said, I will confess my transgressions unto the Lord; and thou forgavest the iniquity of my sin. <long pause>
Notice the order. <short pause> David acknowledged his sin. He didn't hide his iniquity. He confessed. <short pause> And then, in the same verse, the answer comes.
God forgave.

Not after a long wait. <short pause> Not after David proved himself. <short pause> Not after he'd done enough good to balance the scales. <short pause> The moment he brought it into the light, God forgave the iniquity of his sin.
That's how grace works. <short pause> It doesn't wait for you to clean yourself up first. <short pause> It meets you in the mess.
This is the heart of what Jesus did for you. <short pause> He took the guilt you carry, the shame you bury, the record of everything you wish you could erase, and he carried it to the cross.
He didn't die so you could try harder. <short pause> He died so you could be free.
The apostle Paul says it plainly.
There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus, who walk not after the flesh, but after the Spirit. <long pause>

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: No condemnation. <short pause> Not less condemnation. <short pause> Not condemnation on hold until you mess up again. <short pause> No condemnation.
Because you are in Christ Jesus. <short pause> That's not something you earn or lose depending on how well you're doing. <short pause> It's where you are if you've trusted him.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: So what does this mean for you tonight? <short pause> It means you don't have to keep carrying what Jesus already carried. <short pause> You don't have to manage your guilt in the dark, hoping it stays buried. <short pause> You can bring it to him.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Maybe there's something you've been holding for a long time. Something you don't talk about, even in prayer. <short pause> You can name it now, quietly, in your heart. <short pause> Not because God doesn't already know, but because something changes when you stop hiding.
David found that out. <short pause> The psalm doesn't begin with his confession. It begins with the blessing that came after.
Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered. Blessed is the man unto whom the Lord imputeth not iniquity, and in whose spirit there is no guile. <long pause>

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Blessed is the one whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered. <short pause> Blessed is the one to whom the Lord doesn't count iniquity, and in whose spirit there is no deceit.
No more hiding. <short pause> No more pretending. <short pause> No more wasting away under the weight of what you won't say. <short pause> Just the clean, clear relief of being forgiven.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: That's what Jesus offers you tonight. <short pause> Not shame. <short pause> Not a lecture. <short pause> Not a reminder of how far you've fallen. <short pause> Just grace.
Grace that rises higher than any guilt you've buried. <short pause> Grace that says there is no condemnation for you, because you are his.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: So let it go. <short pause> Let him take it. <short pause> He's not surprised by what you've done. He's not shocked by what you carry. <short pause> He already paid for it. <short pause> And he's already forgiven you.
Let's pray. <short pause> Lord Jesus, thank you that your grace is bigger than anything we've buried. Help us rest tonight in the truth that there is no condemnation for us, because we are yours.
Sleep well. You are forgiven.
